rv.q: In Sinyor’s 140 minute comedy revue, we have, alongside Moses, the character of NotMoses – a boy who was also sent down the Nile in a basket but was rejected by the princess for crying too much. A simple twist of fate meant that Moses became a son of the Pharaoh, while NotMoses (do you get it?) became a slave.
NotMoses is a good concept, and – at times – rib-achingly funny. It is also patchy, childish and overlong, and it ultimately collapses under the weight of its own – and our – expectations.
NotMoses is funny and fun, but like the speed of its one liners it's easily forgotten.
